reasons.A: Short declarative sentences, clipped triplets and a plain, brisk tone with little hedging sit far from the author's long, qualified, reflective movement.
reasons.B: Long balanced sentences, an essayistic first person and a dash-framed list match well, but it asserts more flatly and lacks the author's questions and layered hedges.
reasons.C: Opens with a rhetorical question, hedges the way the author does and leans on semicolons and long clauses at about the passage's own density, so it reads closest without overdoing it.
